claims.subject: vp19end_parikshit_kuru
claims.summary: Parīkṣit is named as father of Janamejaya · son of Parīkṣit.

claims.note: Reuses the chapter-19 Parīkṣit anchor. Sanskrit 4.20.1 lists these four sons.

search_log.query: Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.20 Sanskrit Jahnu Suratha and ANU name variants
search_log.outcome: Checked the verse-indexed Sanskrit through 4.20.53. Verse 4.20.2 says “Jahnu’s son was Suratha,” resolving the ANU line’s joined “Janhu Janamejaya” run. Recorded source-form variants for Aśmasārin/Aśmarāviṇ, Ambikā/Ambā, Sarvatraga/Sarvaga, Suhotra/Kuhotra and Kareṇumatī/Reṇumatī.

notes: This batch reuses `vp19end_parikshit_kuru` as the Parīkṣit anchor, `vp19end_jahnu` for Jahnu, and `vp19end_shantanu` for Śāṃtanu, whose narrative continues from the chapter-19 account of his finding Kṛpa and Kṛpī. It also reuses the existing Aśvatthāman node; none is redeclared.

Chapter 20 continues the Śāṃtanu already represented in chapter 19’s Kṛpa/Kṛpī episode, so the existing `vp19end_shantanu` node is reused. Its paternal branch through Pratīpa is recorded from this witness without asserting a broader reconciliation of differing Purāṇic genealogies.

The ANU rendering’s “Janhu Janamejaya” phrase is clarified by Sanskrit 4.20.2, which reads Jahnu’s son Suratha; Janamejaya is separately listed as a son of Parīkṣit in 4.20.1. The four sons are attached to the chapter-19 Parīkṣit anchor.

Several name forms vary between the ANU translation and verse-indexed Sanskrit page. Aśmasārin/Aśmarāviṇ, Ambikā/Ambā, Sarvatraga/Sarvaga, Suhotra/Kuhotra and Kareṇumatī/Reṇumatī are recorded as one named person each with edition variants, not duplicated nodes. Kṛṣṇa-Dvaipāyana and the deity Kṛṣṇa are separate.

Pāṇḍu’s five sons are described as begotten for him through named deities and mothers. Divine begetting and Pāṇḍu’s social/patrilineal father role remain separate. The unnamed serving-girl, king of Kāśī and king of Maṇipura are omitted. Only the named leading sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra are represented; no unnamed groups are connected.

In adjacent chapter 19, ANU renders “Saudāsa Sahadeva” as a combined form, while the Sanskrit text at 4.19.19 separates Saudāsa and Sahadeva. This file keeps the Pāṇḍava Sahadeva as a distinct chapter-20 individual and does not merge him with that chapter-19 line.
